blocking.title: New 'matches no registered catalog' error fires for catalogs that are registered (regression from item 6)
blocking.detail: _cmd_discover_install (extension_install.py about lines 3998-4010) decides this from the CACHED catalogs (load_cached_catalog -> select_catalogs), not from the registered sources. So it fires whenever the cache lags settings: (a) after `source add --catalog /abs/catalog.json` and before `discover --refresh`; (b) when a refresh of that catalog failed; (c) for a hand-edited relative registration whose cache has no registeredAs. In each case it prints "--catalog '<sel>' matches no registered catalog ... 'aelix extension source list' shows them", yet `source list` does show it, and --refresh fixes it. On 751ec582 the same input gave the correct "no catalog entry named X (try: aelix extension discover --refresh)". So round 4 traded one false hint (the srcadd case it fixed) for another, in the plain register-then-install flow. The code comment "Not a stale cache: the selector names no registered catalog, and a refresh would not change that" is false. So is the claim in the commit message, ADR-0255 (A selector that matches no registered catalog says so), and the CHANGELOG. No test covers it: no row checks a registered catalog that has not been refreshed. Related: an absolute selector is matched only by string, so `--catalog <W>/link/catalog.json` (the exact path given to source add, stored resolved as <W>/real/catalog.json; the same happens with macOS /tmp) gets the same error, which itself says 'or a path to its file', while `../link/catalog.json` matches. Suggested fix: decide 'not registered' from settings.get_extension_sources() catalog specs as well as the cache, compare by physical file for absolute selectors too, keep the refresh hint when a registered catalog is missing from the cache, and add a row.
